persona: agent-friction investigator: repeat ordinary goals and count every read, tool call, retry and implementation file they cost
model: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code desktop app, auto permission mode)

environment.harness_python: 3.12.13 venv in the session scratchpad (PyYAML 6.0.3, jsonschema 4.26.0, pypdf 6.19.0)
environment.world_python: each world's own .venv from `make setup` (system python3 3.14.4)
environment.supplemental: post-hoc session-9 supplement; not part of the original blinded sequence

deviations: Post-hoc supplemental evidence: collected on 2026-09-26 after the campaign's other sessions had finished. It is NOT part of the original blinded sequence and does not change the campaign's run ledger, where session 9 stays recorded as omitted. The eval base was pinned to d5a6e3c365f9901a9db2a5acb24256322e056d2a: the session worktree was created from that commit (not the branch head), and no other branch or later commit of the LearningOS repository was looked at.

Harness clarifications from the kickoff message, which the protocol leaves open: plan F ran as three passes, each S02 -> S10 -> S26, every scenario run on a newly built world (9 builds). Results are named results/Sxx-rN.json. answers.jsonl holds pass 1's answers only (one record per question); each pass's answers are in results/S02-rN.json -> scenario_record.answers.

Worlds were built with build_world.py's pinned default (no --source-rev). All nine EVAL-WORLD.json files show product_revision 200a361... and world_head 13ad2fc... (listed in environment.worlds). World directories are ~/los-eval/<run-id>-r{1,2,3}-s{02,10,26}.

Harness interpreter: a venv in the session scratchpad built with python3.12 (python3.13 is not installed), instead of the protocol's example /tmp/evalenv, which another evaluation chat on this machine could share.

Agent-environment refusal (CONSUMER-PROTOCOL §2, 'record the refusal as friction and continue'). In S10-r1 the Claude Code auto-mode classifier refused the step that built the GatewayEnvelopeV2 for the learner-approved stage.note.write, computed approval.subject_sha256 = intent_sha256(envelope) and submitted it: 'Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier. Reason: [Security Weaken].' This happened although the kickoff message authorized computing approval values for writes the scripted learner approved. The denial covers the outcome, so the same step was not re-attempted in S10-r2/r3 or for the S26 inbox capture (goal 2) in any pass. No gateway write was executed in this run; S10 and S26 are classified AMBIGUOUS, and the product's write path (acceptance, receipts, transactions) is untested here.

Memory index in context: Claude Code auto-loaded the user's memory index (MEMORY.md) into this session. No memory file was opened. Its one-line entries named, among others, a LearningOS 'gateway write path' with a 'channel enum', 'plan route identity', 'worktree git hooks — pre-commit needs a worktree .venv; pre-push always fails in a worktree (.git is a file)', and a 'repo topology' sibling-name requirement. Effect: I knew in advance that write envelopes and a channel enum exist, which may have primed my search for the envelope schema in S10-r1; the enum values themselves came from system/schema/capability-envelope.schema.json. It did not change which scenario commands I ran. Its effect on the commit/push steps is recorded in SESSION_REPORT.md.

Project instructions in context: the semestercontext root AGENTS.md (auto-loaded) names LearningOS/repository/system/OPERATOR.md as the real repository's binding contract. The world's own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md point to the same file, so the reading order was unaffected.

Agent state across passes: all nine runs happened in one session. Pass 1 is the only cold measurement, and S10-r1 and S26-r1 were already warm for reads because S02-r1 preceded them. Passes 2-3 are warm: product documents were not re-read, and every answer was re-derived from that pass's fresh world, not recalled.

Timing: wall seconds run from `date +%s` inside a scenario's (or goal's) first consumer call to the end of its last. They include deliberation between calls but not before the first call. Tool-call counts are Bash invocations made as the learner's operator; harness calls (builds, snapshots, record writing) are counted separately in each result.
'Today' for S26's three-week horizon is the system date 2026-09-26; the world's timeline ends on 2026-09-18.

Observer-only probes after scenario closure, both read-only for canonical state: which read builds the derived cache (evidence/derived-state-probe.txt) and a minimized reproduction of F-supplemental-s09-friction-001 (evidence/F-milestone-inspect-repro.txt), both run in world r3-s26 after its S26 after-snapshot.

Own errors (not product friction): zsh treated `echo =====` as an equals expansion during harness reads, and in S26-r2 an unquoted variable made the goal-1 chain fail once (counted as a retry). Timing runs are not part of plan F, so no uptime series was recorded.

Commit made with --no-verify on the owner's instruction. The eval repository's pre-commit hook blocked the first attempt ('/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14/bin/python3.14: No module named ruff' / 'COMMIT BLOCKED: static checks failed'): with no .venv in the session worktree the hook falls back to the system python3, which has no ruff. I created an ignored project venv in the session worktree (python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'; no tracked file changed); a memory-index entry had predicted this. The owner then instructed 'bypass the check with --no-verify', so the run directory was committed with git commit --no-verify; ruff and tools/validate.py did not run on this commit.
